# eslint-plugin-reliability

Guide for AI coding assistants using this plugin in a project. To change the plugin's own source, read https://github.com/ofri-peretz/eslint/blob/main/AGENTS.md instead.

> ESLint reliability rules for runtime safety — enforces error handling, network timeouts, null checks, and safe type narrowing.

## Enable it

```bash
npm install --save-dev eslint-plugin-reliability
```

Requires ESLint ^8.40.0 || ^9.0.0 || ^10.0.0 and Node >=22.13.0.

Flat config files (`eslint.config.*`) are found by ESLint 8.57 and newer; on ESLint 9 and 10 they are the default.

```js
// eslint.config.mjs
import reliability from 'eslint-plugin-reliability';

export default [reliability.configs.recommended];
```

Each preset is one flat config object: put it in the array as an element, do not spread it. Rule ids are prefixed `reliability/`. Add it to the config you already have; do not remove other plugins. TypeScript files need a TypeScript parser in the config (`typescript-eslint`).

## Presets

| Preset        | Rules | Errors | Warnings |
| ------------- | ----- | ------ | -------- |
| `recommended` | 3     | 2      | 1        |

### `recommended`

3 rules:

- `no-silent-errors` (error): Detects empty catch blocks.
- `no-missing-null-checks` (warn): Detects potential null pointer dereferences.
- `require-network-timeout` (error): Require timeout limits for network requests.

### Rules in no preset

Enable these by name (`'reliability/<rule>': 'error'`); README.md describes each: `no-unhandled-promise`, `no-missing-error-context`, `error-message`, `no-unsafe-type-narrowing`, `no-await-in-loop`, `no-jsdoc-terminator-in-example`.
